title: IL-17Rb mediates the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis through STAT6-dependent regulation of TH2 cells and type 2 inflammatory cytokines
abstract: BackgroundAllergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear.ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models.MethodsCandidate genes were screened using GEO datasets…

title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. Machine learning approaches, on the other hand, have been proposed as heuristic surrogates for material fracture, yet they cannot guarantee the physical consistency of the predicted response. To address this shortcoming, we propose the mesoscale neural operator (MNO): a data-driven nonlocal constitutive model that is learned directly from MD loading and displacement data. After training, it can be used in continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and grid sizes. The key idea of the MNO is to exploit the built-in characteristic length of a nonlocal model, called the horizon, to travel across scales. Physical consistency across scales is obtained by building two structural ingredients into the MNO: a normalized kernel that renders the strain energy density invariant under horizon rescaling, and a rescaled critical bond stretch that keeps the energy release rate consistent across scales. Through tests on synthetic data, we show that the MNO and its learning workflow indeed discover the nonlocal continuum multiscale model in the form of the nonlocal kernel and the nonlinear constitutive relation. We then apply the framework to coarse-grained MD data and find that in a test problem, the learned model matches the MD strain energy density and critical energy release rate within 3%. It also predicts the peak transmitted forces within 6% in out-of-distribution tension tests. As a further demonstration, the model is applied to a plate with 4000 times the area of the training specimens and containing an initial defect. In this problem, the model reproduces the main features of dynamic brittle fracture, including branch and cascading branch networks.

title: With the Right Representation, Classical Machine Learning Rivals Deep Models for Olfactory Mixture Similarity
abstract: Modeling olfactory mixtures remains a critical challenge in machine olfaction because the task requires reasoning over relationships between sets of odorants rather than over individual molecules in isolation. However, prior comparisons between deep and classical approaches also varied how the relationship between the two mixtures was represented, since the classical baselines primarily relied on weak representations that described each mixture independently and provided little direct signal about how the mixtures differed. In this work, we revisit classical learning using explicit symmetric comparison features on unordered pairs of mixtures, evaluating these representations with XGBoost and kernel ridge regression (KRR). We find that XGBoost with explicit comparison features achieves performance competitive with specialized deep mixture models on the main benchmark. Ablation studies show that coordinate-wise absolute differences alone provide strong predictive performance, while combining them with sums and products yields further improvements. KRR also benefits substantially from explicit comparison features, with further gains from appropriate kernel choice and preprocessing. Overall, these results suggest that explicitly encoding how two mixtures differ is an important ingredient for classical machine learning in low-data olfactory mixture prediction.

title: Formulation of Brownian chain molecular dynamics and the path-resolved quasi-density operator
abstract: Brownian chain molecular dynamics (BCMD) [M. Shiga, J. Comput. Chem. 43, 1864 (2022)] was introduced as a practical path-integral-based approach to approximate quantum vibrational dynamics in molecular and condensed-phase systems. Its equations of motion combine Newtonian dynamics of the centroid variables with overdamped Brownian dynamics of the non-centroid path variables. Here, we introduce a path-resolved quasi-density-operator (path-QDO) representation by extending the QDO construction underlying centroid molecular dynamics to the full discretized imaginary-time path. For two position-diagonal observables, this representation gives an exact expression for the Kubo-transformed correlation function in the fine-discretization limit, without requiring either observable to be linear. BCMD can be viewed as a phenomenological, time-homogeneous Markov approximation to the exact reduced propagation in these path variables, although its generator is not derived from the path-QDO formulation. We also formulate and validate a multiple-time-step algorithm that allows pseudo-Hamiltonian errors in the deterministic propagation to be controlled by separating the Brownian refresh interval from the inner integration time step. We test the path-QDO representation on one-dimensional models and present BCMD infrared spectra of q-TIP4P/F ice, ambient water, and hot water, comparing them with published results from other approximate quantum-dynamics methods.

title: SG-LegalClarify: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Legal Reasoning and Ambiguity Recognition in Singapore Law
abstract: Singapore offers a distinctive testbed for legal reasoning by large language models (LLMs). Its legal system combines inherited English common law with jurisdiction-specific statutes, requiring models to distinguish local doctrine from generic common-law intuition. This setting also highlights the challenge of recognizing underspecification in lay legal queries, because the facts material to a legal outcome depend on the governing doctrine. Yet legal benchmarks rarely cover Singapore law or test this form of ambiguity recognition. To address these gaps, we introduce SG-LegalClarify, a large-scale benchmark for open-ended legal reasoning and ambiguity recognition in Singapore law. SG-LegalClarify contains 1,100 lawyer-authored source questions spanning 10 legal domains, including 340 fully specified and 760 underspecified questions. Each underspecified question has a fixed hidden-fact assignment and a fully specified counterpart, yielding 1,860 evaluation instances. Responses are graded with lawyer-authored Issue, Rule, Application, and Conclusion (IRAC) rubrics. We evaluate 19 LLMs, closed-book and with web search, using a multi-turn pipeline in which models decide whether to answer or clarify, and a user simulator reveals hidden facts only when asked. We find the benchmark far from saturated: the best models satisfy only 69.8% of mandatory rubric items closed-book (average 53.8%) and 77.8% with web search (average 63.0%). Models also struggle to recognize when clarification is necessary. We will release the public split of our benchmark, the model outputs on it, and the evaluation pipeline to support future research.

title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
abstract: Spallation in ductile materials under high strain rates occurs through the process of void nucleation, growth, and coalescence. Void nucleation is known to depend on factors ranging from microstructural to stress state. The criteria for void nucleation in damage models are stochastic, and microstructural awareness is often neglected. Recently, it was shown that nucleation propensity can be estimated using computer vision. In the present work, this is integrated with a continuum damage model framework for comprehensive simulation of spallation in tantalum under plate impact. Void nucleation probability is governed by a susceptibility field, predicted from grain orientations and grain boundary (GB) energy, with a mechanical barrier set by the local maximum principal stress. This is coupled to a crystal plasticity model within a Lagrangian shock simulation, with microstructure selectively resolved to reduce computational cost. The model is calibrated at a flyer velocity of 196 m/s, where the simulated free surface velocity (FSV) matches experimental measurements of shock arrival, peak state, release and the pullback signal measured in flyer impact experiments, with some deviations confined to the late time ringing. With no further parameter changes, the model transfers to a 214 m/s case and accurately reproduces the FSV. To demonstrate the microstructure-awareness of the nucleation model, a selection of synthetic microstructures is presented for comparison. In the resolved microstructure, voids nucleate predominantly (though not exclusively) at GBs and triple junctions. It is shown that the FSV differs significantly based on the incorporated microstructure, yielding the correct FSV prediction only in the case of representative microstructures.

title: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
abstract: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeration, while the global traversal is securely regulated by an exterior simulated annealing governor augmented by dynamic reheating and continuous elitism caching. We comprehensively benchmarked this classical architecture on the standard HP biophysical lattice against targeted 20-merA, 25-mer, 50-mer, and 64-mer geometries. Most notably, when evaluating the computationally exhaustive 50-mer and 64-mer topologies, the framework successfully bypassed widely accepted heuristic boundaries. By leveraging deterministic exact solving to vault classical energy traps, the system algorithmically resolved a novel, ultra-dense sequence-packing configuration for the 50-mer, defining a new theoretical global optimum.

title: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge and Language Models
abstract: Every medication comes with two types of medical facts: indications, which describe what conditions the drug treats (benefits), and contraindications, which describe who must avoid it to prevent serious harm (safety limits). Although contraindications are critical for patient safety and FDA regulations require listing them as rigorously as indications, we find that contraindications are far less documented than indications in general prose. In this paper, we measure how often these texts contain both facts across 574 drugs from PrimeKG by comparing a drug's indications against its own contraindications. Across Wikipedia articles and PubMed abstracts, we find that reference prose names a drug's benefits about twice as often as its safety limits (within-drug odds ratio 2.19). We call this documentation gap LABEL (Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits). Language models mirror this gap. As we scale Qwen2.5 from 0.5B to 14B, accuracy on indications rises by 18.3 points, whereas accuracy on contraindications remains flat near random guessing. However, when we provide models with a retrieved passage that states the answer, they use safety facts just as effectively as benefits. Furthermore, routing safety questions to official FDA labels boosts accuracy by 15.8 points whenever the label states the fact. Overall, our findings show that models fail on medication safety not because they cannot reason about risk, but because free-text corpora lack safety facts. Clinical AI systems should therefore route medication-safety questions to official regulatory labels and structured databases rather than relying on general public records. Code and data are available at https://github.com/SMRayeed/LABEL.

title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer, a compact hybrid state-space and attention architecture designed for early-life degradation trajectory forecasting. DecayFormer combines cycle-level selective recurrence, using a single scalar state per channel, with an attention mechanism queried by the recurrent state. It further incorporates state-of-charge (SOC) interval statistics and a master curve head that jointly estimates a scalar lifetime and a monotonically non-increasing SOH profile parameterized by normalized lifetime. We evaluate DecayFormer on the BatteryLife benchmark using all 22 aging-condition-exclusive folds, with a single run per fold and one fixed configuration across all folds, without fold-specific tuning. DecayFormer achieves mean test MAPE values of 2.25% on Li-ion, 2.76% on CALB, 0.95% on Na-ion, and 7.19% on Zn-ion. These results demonstrate the potential of compact sequence models to deliver accurate early-life degradation forecasts across diverse battery chemistries and aging conditions, without relying on extensive model scaling or per-fold optimization.

title: Learning inadequacy of Bayesian neural operators for PDE-constrained inference and design
abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin predictive modeling across science, engineering and medicine. Their use in digital twins, parameter inference and optimal design requires repeated solutions across parameters and scenarios. For nonlinear, transient and multiphysics systems, these calculations can make numerical simulation prohibitively expensive. Here we introduce the residual-informed Bayesian neural operator (RI-BNO), which learns operator inadequacy using a posteriori error estimates from the governing PDEs and incorporates its correction and uncertainty into Bayesian training and prediction. We establish local error bounds for the residual-informed estimates under stability and smoothness assumptions. We demonstrate RI-BNO on a non-linear reaction-diffusion benchmark with DeepONet and latent-subspace architectures, Markov chain Monte Carlo inference of glioma parameter fields from magnetic resonance imaging, and Monte Carlo risk-averse optimization of three-dimensional thermal breaks in building envelopes under manufacturing uncertainty. Across the evaluated examples, RI-BNO improves agreement with finite element (FE) reference predictions, parameter posteriors and optimized designs while using half as many full nonlinear or transient training simulations as the vanilla Bayesian neural operator (vBNO). For thermal break design, online optimization time decreases from 178 hours with the FE model to 18 minutes with RI-BNO. These results demonstrate the value of explicit inadequacy modeling in neural operators for reliable PDE-based inference and design.

title: Efficient simulation of the generalized Langevin equation using a basis of dynamically relevant histories for memory and noise
abstract: The Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) is a cornerstone for modeling non-Markovian dynamics, but its numerical solution remains challenging due to the history-dependent convolution and the need to generate colored noise with a prescribed correlation function. We introduce a forward construction that addresses both challenges within a single framework. We represent an arbitrary trajectory as sum of relevant and irrelevant parts, where relevant part can be decomposed into a small number of characteristic history patterns that make the main contribution to future dynamics. It allows to reduce numerical cost to \(O(d^2)\) for $d$ chosen patterns instead of full history. The same construction applies to colored noise generation, where the causal filter plays the role of the memory kernel. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method for several representative kernels, including long-range kernels with power-law tails.

title: Beyond the Exchange Picture of Singlet–Triplet Gaps
abstract: Molecules with inverted singlet–triplet gaps are promising candidates for next-generation organic light-emitting diode emitters, but identifying general principles that explain and guide singlet–triplet inversion remains challenging. Here, we investigate substituted heptazines, vibrational ensembles of azupyrene and isopyrene, and a chemically diverse molecular set using CIS, EOM-CCSD, and wave function-based state matching.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. The result is a single set of end-to-end-trained weights that simultaneously performs all tasks and surpasses state-of-the-art models specialized for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation. Our results demonstrate the viability of scaling generalist decoder-only models for native multimodal understanding and generation across language and chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/the-matter-lab/nahual.

title: Interplay of interfacial energetics and selective Ni segregation in the morphology of co-precipitates in low-alloy steels
abstract: Coupled precipitation and interfacial segregation in low-alloy steels change precipitate stability and morphology, which influence strengthening and embrittlement. Cu-rich precipitates (CRPs) and Mn-Ni-Si-rich precipitates (MNSPs) frequently form core-shell or appendage morphologies, but the interfacial energetics controlling this change are not well quantified. We combine a density-functional-theory-trained cluster expansion with lattice Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the Fe/CRP, Fe/MNSP and Cu/MNSP interfaces within one Hamiltonian. The three coefficients based on excess internal energy follow gamma_Cu/MNSP < gamma_Fe/CRP <~ gamma_Fe/MNSP and give a positive work of adhesion and a negative spreading parameter, consistent with favorable Mn-Ni-Si attachment to a CRP and partial coverage. Only Ni segregates to the Fe/CRP boundary. Mn and Si segregate weakly on their own but become more enriched when Ni is present and co-segregate with Ni at the boundary. Ni forms an interfacial layer about one monolayer thick with an excess of 7.4-9.6 atoms/nm^2, develops B2-like local order and shows an energy reduction that increases with Ni coverage. At 1 at.% matrix Ni, a Gibbs adsorption analysis gives a Fe/CRP free-energy reduction of about 0.15 J/m^2. These interface coefficients and segregation trends connect segregation, interface energy and co-precipitation and support compositional optimization in low-alloy steels.

title: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
abstract: Closed-loop experimentation requires more than selecting the next experiment. It must also determine which existing measurements and model-derived relationships are sufficiently supported to influence that decision. Here we introduce SPARC (Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components), a framework that continually revises this support as experimental evidence accumulates. Competing model families are evaluated through out-of-fold predictions, so that each model is tested on observations not used in its corresponding fit. Sparse posterior composition assigns model influence according to predictive contributions supported by the out-of-fold evidence, retaining complementary contributions from several model families. Candidate-dependent predictive dispersion and residual variability define trust, which modulates exploration alongside the predicted response. Independent diagnostics also prioritize existing measurements for prospective verification, with model-derived trust reported alongside them. Across eight published materials datasets, SPARC achieved higher $R^2$ than the corresponding literature-reported values in six, with relative gains of up to 77% without the density-functional-theory- or experiment-derived descriptors used by several published pipelines. In an automated alkaline oxygen-evolution-reaction campaign, 8 of 11 SPARC-selected experiments reached overpotentials below 300 mV, with a best value of 242 mV, compared with 18 of 125 initial experiments. Measurements prioritized for verification before repetition subsequently deviated by 76 mV on average, compared with 27 mV for matched controls. SPARC therefore turns experimental evidence into a basis for revising model influence, directing exploration and identifying measurements that warrant verification.

title: Emergence of Anisotropic Defect Networks in Shocked Diamond
abstract: Predicting failure after shock loading requires understanding how the structures created during compression evolve as the material unloads. In diamond, both crystal plasticity and localized amorphization have been reported to accommodate shock-induced shear. However, it remains unresolved how the resulting defect structures organize in three dimensions during compression and how this organization influences where tensile damage localizes during release. Here we couple phase-contrast-enhanced radiography at an X-ray free-electron laser with simulations to address this question in single-crystal diamond. By combining radiographs at multiple pump-probe delays with hydrodynamic calculations, we show that linear features first become visible behind the plastic wavefront while material near the front remains highly compressed. By rotating the viewing direction about the shock axis, we find that the projected feature angles favor finite $\{111\}$ sheets elongated along in-plane directions close to $\langle112\rangle$. Molecular dynamics simulations show that an interconnected network of amorphous bands and stacking faults forms during compression, preferentially on $\{111\}$ variants with larger in-plane shear traction. Projections of this network qualitatively reproduce the observed loss of feature visibility with rotation. During simulated release, tension opens local cracks within these pre-existing amorphous bands. These results support a pathway in which the crystallographically organized defect network formed during compression provides preferred sites for tensile damage during release. This pathway may also operate in other strongly covalent solids.

title: Flat-band driven bipolar anomalous Nernst effect towards volt-scale transverse thermoelectric conversion
abstract: Unipolar anomalous Nernst thermopiles are critically plagued by metallic interconnects, which induce heavy Joule dissipation and compromise the module's packing density, ultimately capping voltage generation. Here, we circumvent these limitations by establishing an intrinsic bipolar anomalous Nernst effect (BANE) paradigm, enabling seamless series integration analogous to Seebeck n-p pairs without passive metallic bridges. Focusing on flat-band topological systems, through machine learning assisted screening across multiple target properties, we identified 249 BANE materials, exhibiting near-room-temperature polarity switching. Guided by this predictive framework, we experimentally realized this phenomenon in single crystals of the Weyl ferromagnet, Co$_2$TiGe. Strikingly, while its intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) remains rigorously temperature-invariant up to the Curie temperature, the anomalous Nernst signal undergoes a sharp polarity inversion across $T \approx 225$ K. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to the interplay between flat bands and Weyl nodes, where thermal depopulation shifts the chemical potential across the band edge, inverting the sign of $\partial σ_{xy} / \partial ε$ via the Mott relation. This work opens an avenue toward compact, monolithic transverse thermopiles capable of volt-scale generation free from interfacial parasitic dissipation.

title: A Multigrid Finite State Projection Algorithm For The Solution Of The Reaction-Diffusion Master Equation
abstract: We develop a multigrid method for the finite state projection of the reaction-diffusion master equation (RDME). The RDME evolves the joint probabilities of molecular count configurations across well-mixed voxels coupled by local reactions and diffusive jumps. When fast diffusion or large reaction rates make this evolution stiff over long time horizons, implicit time stepping requires solving a large shifted linear system at every step. Grouping neighboring voxels and summing their molecular counts produces a hierarchy of coarser state spaces terminating at a one-voxel chemical master equation. Restriction sums residual entries with the same coarse counts, while multinomial prolongation preserves the RDME generator form on every level with explicit coarse reaction and diffusion rates. For reversible diffusion, the error omitted by coarsening is bounded by the graph Dirichlet energy of jumps inside the aggregates, with a constant independent of population. Numerical tests with standard multigrid cycles and point or block Gauss-Seidel smoothing reach 7.16 million states and resolve rare probabilities of order $10^{-7}$.

title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 μm. The continuous electroluminescent interface also reproduces complex contact patterns without computational reconstruction of electrical fields. Direct lamination of the ACEL device onto a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor is expected to enable compact contact imaging in an assembly less than 5 mm thick, substantially thinner than conventional vision-based tactile sensors. This approach could reduce the space required for high-resolution tactile imaging, offering greater design freedom for dexterous robotic hands.

title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
abstract: Molecular dynamics is an extremely powerful approach for studying protein behavior, but it requires enormous computational resources to obtain an adequate sampling of possible conformations. Recently, thanks to successes in predicting three-dimensional protein structures, there has been an explosion of research exploring the opportunities offered by deep learning to address the problem of protein conformational landscape. In this work, an artificial intelligence system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture is introduced and applied to the problem of determining the ensemble of three-dimensional structures that a protein can access and their statistical weight. After being trained on a dataset of conformations of a particular protein obtained using classical all-atom molecular dynamics, this neural network is able to directly generate physically plausible protein conformations similar to those obtained both through molecular dynamics and experimentally. The ordered sequence of conformations obtained as output of the neural network rapidly converges towards the most populated regions of the protein's conformational landscape, suggesting that the system may have learned not only the protein's three-dimensional organization but also the thermodynamic weights of the various feasible conformations. These features, combined with its simplicity and low computational load, make this Transformer variant an ideal candidate for the development of systems capable of performing generative molecular dynamics.

title: From Mutation to Medication: Characterizing Failures of Clinical LLMs to Respect Genomic Resistance
abstract: Language models are increasingly proposed to support molecular tumour boards, but may recommend cancer therapies despite genomic evidence of resistance. We evaluated ten models on 1,464 resistance cases from five curated oncology knowledge bases, collecting 58,910 judgments. Models endorsed resisted therapies in 21.8-81.4% of cases. However, raw rates can reflect a tendency to agree rather than an ability to distinguish resistance from drug sensitivity: one open-weight model endorsed 81.4% of resistance cases and 82.3% of sensitivity controls. We therefore compared endorsement within matched gene and evidence-level groups. This analysis is exploratory because it was specified after the pre-registered analysis, which yielded null-to-weak results. Measured failures depended strongly on the reference knowledge base and evidence strength. When a second source independently confirmed resistance, four models across three vendors endorsed at most 2.4% of cases; at weaker evidence tiers, discrimination was not measurable. Models sometimes acknowledged resistance yet recommended the therapy. Repeating a model's own resistance conclusion reduced endorsement to 0.0-3.5% on cases where it had stated resistance. Falsely attributing the opposite conclusion increased endorsement above baseline for all seven hosted models, reaching 95.2% for GPT-4o; an instruction without an attributed conclusion changed endorsement by only 0.9 percentage points. Providing the correct curated evidence reduced unqualified strong recommendations to 0.3-3.5%, testing evidence use under an oracle condition rather than retrieval.

title: Exploring Energy Landscapes for Functional Materials: Ga vacancies in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$
abstract: Energy landscape exploration requires extensive energy and force evaluations, making efficient access to interatomic potentials an important practical challenge. We present a persistent socket interface that connects the landscape exploration tools in the GMIN, OPTIM, and PATHSAMPLE programs to potentials available through the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE). The persistent design keeps both the calculator and socket connection active throughout the search, avoiding repeated initialisation. We apply this framework to understand and predict the properties of Ga vacancies in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ using two NequIP-based potentials, and construct kinetic transition networks describing complex vacancy configurations and migration pathways. Temperature-dependent analysis of the dominant paths reveals how the most probable migration sequence can change, with the mechanism governed by global properties of the network, rather than simply the highest energy barrier. Visualisation, mean first-passage times, and heat capacities enable us to connect the organisation of the landscape to relaxation time scales and thermodynamic observables. The interface extends energy landscape methods to ASE-compatible atomistic models, providing a general framework for combining global optimisation, transition state searches, kinetic network analysis, and thermodynamic characterisation with recent developments in machine-learned interatomic potentials.

title: A multimodal model integrating microscopic images and fractal dimension for characterizing the granulation process of aerobic granular sludge
abstract: Reliable identification of aerobic granular sludge (AGS) granulation stages can support cultivation monitoring and operational adjustment. We collected 231 microscopic images and particle size measurements from three sequencing batch reactors operated at influent chemical oxygen demand concentrations of 250, 500, and 1000 mg/L. Growth, stabilization, and disintegration were labeled according to consecutive-day changes in median particle diameter (ΔD50). Agreement between expert consensus and threshold-based labels was 88.31% (Cohen's κ = 0.823).

title: Topology-Based Generation of Hypothetical Metal−Organic Frameworks through Single-Metal Nodes and Symmetry-Aware Linker Rotation
abstract: Topology-based hypothetical metal−organic framework (MOF) generators enable scalable exploration of chemical space beyond experimentally reported structures, but their accessible design space is constrained by the building blocks and assembly rules they encode. Here, we present PORMAKE2, an upgraded topology-based hypothetical MOF generator designed to improve both access to small-pore structures and geometric fidelity. PORMAKE2 introduces an expanded building-block library, including single-metal nodes, and implements symmetry-aware linker rotation for higher-fidelity framework assembly.

title: Heavier-than-expected electron behavior may explain slower electrical flow in alpha-gallium oxide
abstract: Power electronic devices help control the flow of electricity and convert it into forms needed by different machines, such as electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and industrial equipment. Some electrical energy is lost as heat during this process, reducing efficiency and potentially affecting the device's performance. Semiconductor materials that can withstand high voltages, carry electricity efficiently and release heat effectively would make these devices more efficient and reliable.

title: A Stable and Highly Selective Sodium Solid-State ElectrolyteHigh-Energy Mechanochemical Treatment of Disodium Dodecahydridododecaborate
abstract: Fast, stable, and low-cost solid electrolytes are essential for advancing all-solid-state sodium batteries. Here, we present a fast solid-state sodium ion conductor, which reaches an ionic conductivity of σ(Na+) = 2.8 × 10−3 S cm−1 at 60 °C with an activation energy of Ea = 0.393 eV, made by high-energy mechanochemical treatment of disodium dodecahydrido-closo-dodecaborate, Na2B12H12. The milling process facilitates a transition to the high-temperature dynamically disordered β-polymorph while also providing high stability toward thermal cycling in the range RT to 300 °C.

title: Identification of Key Fatty acid Metabolism-Related Genes in Vascular Dementia
abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD.

title: From Thermal Thresholds to Temporal Response: A Dual-Dimension Framework for Lithium-Ion Battery Safety
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face a persistent safety challenge from thermal runaway (TR), a catastrophic failure triggered by exothermic chain reactions under abuse conditions. Despite extensive progress in material-level thermal stabilization, most strategies remain confined to raising temperature thresholds, overlooking the temporal dimension of TR progression. This review introduces a temperature-time dual-dimensional framework that unifies TR mechanisms, characterization techniques, and mitigation strategies. We first elucidate the TR process and put forward key parameters.

title: From Molecular Structure to Human Pharmacokinetics: Clearance Prediction Drives Exposure Error in a Hybrid ML–PBPK Workflow
abstract: End-to-end structure-to-exposure workflows combine molecular representation, pharmacokinetic (PK) input prediction, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulation, but aggregate accuracy does not reveal where error enters the workflow. We developed graph-based models for predicting plasma unbound fraction, systemic clearance, and steady-state volume of distribution and used paired input substitution in fixed compound-specific PBPK models to trace the downstream effects of these predictions. On held-out benchmark sets, models combining graph-derived and physicochemical features performed comparably to descriptor-based controls, with no detectable paired differences. In 41 compounds, replacing observed clearance with predicted intrinsic or systemic clearance caused the largest deterioration in exposure prediction. AUC0–t 2-fold coverage decreased from 82.9% to between 41.5 and 53.7%, whereas substitutions of physicochemical properties, plasma unbound fraction, and volume of distribution had smaller effects. The intrinsic-clearance and systemic-clearance workflows were not detectably different under matched input slots. Persistent Cmax underprediction with observed inputs indicated an additional limitation in distribution-model structure. When all three PK inputs were predicted, AUC0–t and Cmax were within 2-fold for 41 and 59% of compounds. Because encoder exposure may favor performance in this set, these coverage estimates are upper bounds for unseen chemistry. The paired-substitution design therefore identifies limited clearance prediction accuracy, rather than the PBPK clearance parametrization strategy, as the principal source of exposure error in the evaluated workflow and separates it from residual PBPK structural error.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Dual-database pharmacovigilance analysis based on FAERS and JADER combined with network pharmacology to explore fulvestrant-associated respiratory toxicity
abstract: BackgroundFulvestrant serves as cornerstone endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive (HR-positive) advanced breast cancer. Recent reports indicate safety concerns regarding respiratory toxicity. This study systematically characterized fulvestrant-related respiratory adverse events (adverse events, AEs) using two independent spontaneous reporting databases (FAERS and JADER) for cross-verification and investigated underlying mechanisms.MethodsDisproportionality analysis utilized two post-marketing surveillance databases, the United States Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event…
venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

title: An Alternative Superoxide-Mediated Pathway for Flavin-Dependent Oxidative Dechlorination in HcbA1
abstract: Flavin-dependent monooxygenases typically activate molecular oxygen through flavin-peroxide intermediates. In HcbA1, however, aerobic oxidative dechlorination of hexachlorobenzene (HCB) is accompanied by the formation of flavin-N5-oxide (FlN5O), raising the question of how oxygen activation is coupled to substrate dechlorination and oxidation. Here, we use multiscale computational approaches, including structural analysis, molecular dynamics simulations, density functional theory, and QM/MM calculations, to evaluate the feasibility of an alternative superoxide-mediated pathway.

title: Alkyl Side-Chain and Ionic-Block Design of Mixed-Charge Polyurethane Copolymer Hydrogels: from Nanostructure and Viscoelasticity to Thermo-Optical and Mechanical Properties
abstract: Mixed-charge polyurethane (MCPU) copolymers with tunable alkyl side chains (C1, C6, and C18) and ionic-block ratios (60% and 70%) were synthesized and assembled into single-network (SN) physical hydrogels. Three different nanostructures were identified by small-angle X-ray scattering: weakly segregated domains (C1), periodic microphase separation (C6), and microphase separation with interdigitated lamellar ordering (C18). Rheology studies provide a macroscopic relaxation timescale (τrelax) that quantifies the rate of noncovalent network rearrangement.

title: Directional Nitrite Spillover Couples to Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks for Ampere-Level Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia is often constrained by the proton-coupled hydrogenation of adsorbed nitrite (*NO2), a step commonly accelerated through hydrogen spillover and local reactive-hydrogen (*H) supply. This hydrogen-centered view, however, treats *NO2 largely as a passive intermediate and overlooks whether its migration can reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bond-network environment required for downstream hydrogenation. Here, we show that directional *NO2 spillover couples site-specific intermediate transport with interfacial hydrogen-bond-network reorganization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies early stage breast cancer subclasses from aberrant glycogene expression and informs personalised drug treatment.
abstract: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering of early-stage breast cancer glycogene expression data using the Growing Hierarchical Self Organising Representation Map (GHSORM) algorithm identified seven subclasses. These glycogene expression clusters (GECs) overlap with known breast cancer biomarkers such as hormone receptor status and immune signatures. Feature discovery via Recursive Feature Elimination with Strikeout (RFES) identified a panel of 60 glycogenes that can predict GECs on an independent testing set with 90.48% accuracy.

title: Sex, but not age, drives transcriptome-wide gene expression variation in a turtle with female-biased longevity
abstract: Sexes frequently differ in life-history traits including body size, lifespan, and age at sexual maturity. Organismal aging, the progressive decline in physiological function and cellular resilience over time, is a central component of sex-specific life histories, yet the mechanisms driving sex differences in aging remain largely unresolved. Long-term mark-recapture efforts reveal a striking pattern of female-biased longevity in painted turtles (Chrysemys picta) (lifespan: males = 24 years, females = 48 years).

title: Tuning molten pool dynamics and keyhole formation during laser powder bed fusion through laser beam shaping
abstract: Tuning molten pool dynamics and keyhole formation during laser powder bed fusion through laser beam shaping

title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

title: An AI-designed, recombinantly produced FtsZ-directed peptide with in vitro activity against pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is outpacing the antibiotic pipeline, yet antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) - the most-cited alternative class - remain constrained by proteolytic instability, host toxicity, and the cost of solid-phase synthesis. We report an integrated design-to-validation pipeline that addresses these constraints and yields a de novo peptide directed at an intracellular, non-lytic target.

title: Non-B DNA Finder: A Unified Computational Framework for High-Throughput Detection and Contextual Analysis of Noncanonical DNA Structures in Diverse Genomes
abstract: Noncanonical DNA secondary structures arise from unique sequence patterns, and their formation in vivo is modulated by local genomic context, including DNA supercoiling, chromatin state, and transcriptional activity. They contribute fundamentally to DNA replication, transcription dynamics, genome organization, gene regulation, genetic diversity, genome instability, disease pathogenesis, and aging. However, current computational tools for non-B DNA detection are limited in scope. Most predict only one or a few structural classes.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Cross-Selective Alkyl–Alkyl Negishi Coupling at Isolable, High-Spin ( S = 3/2) Cobalt(II)–Alkyl Catalysts
abstract: A high-spin (S = 3/2) cobalt(II)–dialkyl complex supported by the weak-field ligand N,N,N’,N’-tetramethylethylenediamine (TMEDA) served as a precatalyst for alkyl–alkyl Negishi cross-coupling of alkyl bromide electrophiles. Organometallic studies indicated the isolability of the cross-coupling resting state (TMEDA)cobalt(II)–monoalkyl bromide complex, which was resistant against deleterious β-hydride elimination due to the high-spin (S = 3/2) electronic configuration disfavoring β-agostic H-to-Co interactions.

title: Sequence-Regulated Adhesion of Poly(diethyl glycolide- alt -β-butyrolactone) Synthesized via Enantiomorphic Site-Assisted Stereospecific Alternating Copolymerization
abstract: Biodegradable polyesters can be promising adhesives for their inherent biodegradability, yet their adhesive performance still requires substantial enhancement to meet practical demands. In this work, the alternating sequence effect on adhesive property was explored in the alternating copolymer of S,S-diethylglycolide (S,S-EG, derived from α-hydroxybutyric acid, i.e., α-ethyl-glycolic acid) and R-β-butyrolactone (R-BBL, derived from β-hydroxybutyric acid).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Scalable recorders of cellular calcium dynamics and molecular interactions across time
abstract: Cellular processes are mediated by dynamic biochemical events in their native context, including changes in intracellular ion concentrations and transient interactions between molecules. Studying these processes across large cell populations requires recording their dynamics across time in single cells, simultaneously and at scale. Here, we introduce split-1POK, a split protein tape monomer whose two halves reconstitute when the domains fused to them interact. The reconstituted monomer is incorporated into the protein tape as it elongates across time in live cells, enabling scalable, spatiotemporally resolved endpoint readout under conventional light microscopy. Split-1POK provides a programmable scaffold for new recorders in the CytoSense family, our previously introduced framework (ref. 1) in which the same cytosol-localized monomer senses cellular activity and writes it along protein tape recorders. Unlike transcription-based activity recorders, which encode the signal through new gene expression, CytoSense recorders act on monomers post-synthesis, so the activity signal is sensed and written directly in the cytosol without passing through transcription- or translation-associated cascades. Fusing calmodulin and its binding peptide to split-1POK, we built TCaMP (Tape monomer-CalModulin-Peptide), a genetically encoded calcium recorder (GECR) that measures calcium dynamics on a single, analog intensity scale along a continuous time axis, providing quantitative comparison of calcium levels over time within the same cell. In cultured human cells, TCaMP records transient calcium dynamics from transmembrane entry, receptor activation, and intracellular store release, detecting stimulations as brief as ten minutes. With hour-scale kinetics over days, TCaMP complements fluorescent calcium indicators by trading sub-second temporal resolution for scalable, long-term recording. Fusing conditional dimerization pairs to split-1POK yields recorders of molecular interaction histories in response to external stimuli. Split-1POK thus brings scalable, spatiotemporally resolved recording to intracellular calcium dynamics and molecular interactions across time.

title: From features to digital biomarkers: EEG-fNIRS classification pipelines for brain monitoring
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. This review provides a structured overview of EEG- and fNIRS-based classification studies, with a particular focus on signal processing workflows and biomarker extraction. The reviewed literature is organized around key stages of the analytical pipeline, including target formulation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Common feature families-spanning spectral, temporal, connectivity-based, network-level, and hemodynamic representations-are summarized and discussed in relation to their typical applications and limitations. The main contribution is an evidence-based distinction between signal features and credible candidate biomarkers. Reliability, analytical robustness, external generalization, and interpretability are considered within the intended context of use. Clinical utility is assessed separately from predictive performance. Across 117 primary studies, most measures remained candidate biomarkers; only four studies were assigned to independent clinical validation, with qualifications, and none evaluated clinical utility.

title: Advanced drug delivery strategies for overcoming tumor-mediated molecular hijacking: Emerging nanotherapeutics, advanced biotherapeutics, and artificial intelligence
abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling.

title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
abstract: Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: The Oxygen Reduction Reaction over Pt Nanoparticles Studied with First-Principles-Based Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction is essential to reduce the dependence on fossil fuels. Although widely studied, the underlying reason for the onset overpotential of the reaction over Pt-based nanoparticles remains debated. Here, a first-principles-based kinetic Monte Carlo framework is developed to elucidate the main reaction mechanism, rate-determining steps, and the reason for the overpotential. Effects of the aqueous environment with directional hydrogen bonds are incorporated in the kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, and a framework for simulating linear sweep voltammetry is presented. We find that the overpotential originates from the high coverages of oxygen species (*O, *OH, and *H2O), which block sites for O2 adsorption. The kinetic simulations demonstrate that the effects of site-blocking can be tuned by the shape and size of the Pt nanoparticles. The lowest overpotential is obtained for particles in the size range between 3 and 6 nm with large fractions of (111) facets. The developed methods are general and facilitate the understanding and optimization of catalysts used in a range of electrochemical reactions.

title: Secondary Sphere Modification Tunes C–OH Bond Cleavage and Redistributes Rate Control in Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction by Molecular Cr Complexes
abstract: Mitigating the contribution of anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions to global climate change has motivated the development of earth-abundant transition-metal catalysts capable of electrochemically reducing CO2 to value-added chemical products. It has previously been demonstrated that bipyridine-based CrN2O2 complexes can selectively reduce CO2 to carbon monoxide (CO) under electrochemical conditions. To improve the kinetic parameters (turnover frequency) of this catalyst family, the effect of adding –OMe pendent substituents to the bipyridine backbone of the ligand structure was explored. Here, two catalysts bearing different numbers and positions of –OMe pendent groups are reported and analyzed with respect to their impact on the proton-transfer step that accompanies C–OH bond cleavage as a part of the catalytic cycle for CO2 reduction. Combining the observed isotope effect for each catalyst with an intrinsic value computed for that catalyst resolves the contributions of CO2 binding and C–OH bond cleavage to rate control individually, giving varying degrees of rate control for CO2 binding across the series. Separating the underlying rate constants shows that, across the series, the rate constant for C–OH cleavage varies by about two orders of magnitude, whereas that for CO2 binding varies by less than a factor of two. This work suggests that the addition of –OMe groups can provide a kinetic enhancement compared to complexes without the substituents; however, the benefit is tempered by shared rate control with the CO2 binding step of the reaction, which was previously shown to contribute to the observed rate.

title: A new chemical network to explore the disequilibrium chemistry of silicates and iron in hot gas giants
abstract: Chemical equilibrium modeling of gas giant planet atmospheres has shown that the production and condensation of silicates plays an important role in shaping their final composition. However, no chemical kinetics network for these species are available, preventing the opportunity to analyze the impact of chemical disequilibrium processes. In this paper we present \texttt{SILANE}, a new chemical network that include Mg, Si, Fe and 15 carriers of these elements, including MgSiO$_3$ and Mg$_2$SiO$_4$, ready for use in the VULCAN code. We compare the results of our network with a chemical equilibrium model and discuss them in relation to previous results from literature. We then apply our new network to the analysis of a vertically mixed, Solar-composition atmosphere with equilibrium temperatures $T_{eq}$ in the [700, 1600] K range, finding that (i) rock-forming silicates disappears from the upper atmosphere already at 1100 K, (ii) SiH$_4$ reaches concentrations of $10^{-7}$ in the upper ($P\le 1.0$ bar) atmosphere for planets with $T_{eq}\in$ [800, 1100] K and (iii) the amount of oxygen in refractories decrease from 21\% at $T_{eq}$=700 K to essentially zero already at 1000 K, while in the classical equilibrium framework it remains constant up to $T_{eq}$=1300 K. By applying our network to the case of the young hot Jupiter YSES-1 c and comparing both the mixing ratios of volatile species and the enstatite fraction in the silicate mix, we find evidence of a well-mixed atmosphere, possibly with an average $K_{zz} \ge 10^{10}$ cm$^{2}$s$^{-1}$ up to the $10^{-4}$ bar level.

title: Machine Learning-Driven ZnO NRs@Ag SERS Platform for Rheumatoid Arthritis Liquid Biopsy in a Multicenter-Recruited Cohort
abstract: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment.

title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. Our results establish an electrically programmable, non-volatile magnon transistor.

title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. Forward and inverse neural networks, and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model were trained on subsets of 10 to 10,000 samples. All models exhibited power-law scaling, with prediction errors decreasing with dataset size. Experimental inverse-design validation showed that larger datasets produced spectra closer to a broadband-emitter target. The diffusion model generated multiple candidate parameter sets, allowing selection among alternative solutions based on ease of fabrication, cost, and scalability. These results demonstrate predictable learning-curve scaling in non-ideal experimental data and provide a quantitative basis for estimating the benefit of additional experimental data, and thus the cost-effectiveness of materials-informatics.

title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
abstract: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $μ$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

title: Affordable Analytic Gradients for G0W0-BSE Excited States for Multiple GW Variants via Back-Propagation
abstract: We derive, implement and validate analytic nuclear gradients for three variants of $GW$ self-energies---the contour-deformation (CD), the analytic continuation (AC), and the contour deformation with $W$-analytic-continuation (CD-WAC)---and for the Bethe--Salpeter equation (BSE) built on top of them. All gradients are expressed as contractions of a set of covectors connected to derivatives of primitive quantities in SCF calculations. The derivation of these covectors is a back-propagation procedure through the $GW$ and BSE equations. Central finite differences confirm the correctness of all implemented gradients. With the AC-$GW$-BSE gradient we optimize the excited-state geometries of carbon monoxide, a donor-acceptor dye labelled as DA1, and DMABN, a typical model system for twisted intramolecular charge-transfer phenomena (TICT), and have obtained results that successfully reproduce observations from experiments or high-level calculations. We also performed trajectory surface hopping (TSH) simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) of DMABN using the SHARC NAMD package, showing the capacity of our method to simulate NAMD problems. We performed timing and memory scaling tests, demonstrating that the gradient calculations of both $GW$ and BSE scale asymptotically as $N^4$ for timing and $N^3$ for memory. All source codes used in the present work, including the REST program package and the modified SHARC NAMD package that supports REST as the quantum chemistry backend, are available on Gitee https://gitee.com/restgroup/rest and https://gitee.com/qirui-gao-2025/sharc

title: Tracking gas-solid hydration kinetics by non-contact in situ transflection micro-FTIR spectroscopy
abstract: Gas--solid reaction kinetics is important in applications such as thermochemical heat storage (TCHS), but experimental evaluation remains a bottleneck in materials development. This study evaluates non-contact \textit{in situ} transflection micro-Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy for tracking hydration reactions between water vapor and inorganic solids. Powder layers of La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, CaSO$_4$, and CaO, exhibiting different hydration mechanisms and kinetics, were deposited on an Au-coated glass substrate and exposed to humidified N$_2$. Evolution of water- and hydroxyl-related IR absorption band areas was compared with thermogravimetry (TG)-derived hydration numbers. The FTIR band-area profiles were broadly consistent with the TG-derived hydration trends, showing close agreement for La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and CaSO$_4$. For CaO, some differences were observed between the FTIR and TG results, possibly because CaO is sensitive to differences in gas-phase conditions, particularly the initial increase in humidity, between the two measurements. The spectra distinguished molecular-water uptake in La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and CaSO$_4$ from hydroxide formation in CaO. They also detected carbonate formation during CaO hydration. Thus, \textit{in situ} time-resolved FTIR separately monitored individual chemical reactions, whereas TG recorded only their combined effect on the sample mass. These results demonstrate the potential of transflection micro-FTIR for chemically selective monitoring of gas--solid reactions in small localized samples.

title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, yet existing evaluations provide limited assurance that they behave consistently with their intended characteristics across diverse interactions. We introduce an evaluation framework for measuring the behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents. The framework operationalizes agent behavior along five measurable axes and uses a standardized evaluation battery spanning six socially salient interaction settings to assess behavioral differentiation, consistency, and drift. Controlled persona configurations serve as experimental anchors, enabling systematic testing of whether intended behavioral differences persist across contexts rather than appearing only as stylistic variation. Preliminary analyses demonstrate measurable differentiation across configurations and suggest associations between behavioral profiles and interaction outcomes. By shifting the focus from persona design to behavioral assurance, this work provides a foundation for evaluating whether socially deployed AI agents behave as intended, consistently and measurably, across the situations in which users encounter them.

title: Bright-Dark State Interplay Governs Vibronic Decoherence in Molecular Aggregates
abstract: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates. Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation. Remarkably, states with different excitation energies exhibit nearly identical purity dynamics when their local relaxation networks are similar. The resulting H--J asymmetry further reveals the importance of energetic directionality. These findings establish a reliable connection between optical spectroscopy, vibronic band structure, and state-selective loss in purity.

title: Hydration-induced local diffusivity heterogeneity modulates aqueous $H_2+OH$ reaction kinetics
abstract: At room temperature, a Kramers reaction rate calculated with homogeneous solvent friction exceeds the measured rate of the aqueous reaction $H_2 + OH -> H + H_2O$ by about an order of magnitude. We show that spatially correlated hydration-induced diffusivity fluctuations increase effective friction and suppress the predicted escape rate. Estimates based on hydration-shell properties bring the theoretical rate closer to experiment. The suppression weakens with increasing temperature, linking local solvent heterogeneity to activated aqueous reaction kinetics.

title: Federated versus Centralized PV Capacity-Factor Forecasting: A Non-Inferiority Study Across Seven Stations in North Macedonia
abstract: Background: Photovoltaic (PV) forecasts inform energy commitments by PV operators and aggregators and guide charge-discharge scheduling in solar-plus-storage systems. Federated learning enables collaborative model training through model updates when local operators cannot pool raw operational data. This study evaluated whether federated training was non-inferior to centralized training for PV capacity-factor prediction across seven stations in North Macedonia. A common multilayer perceptron was used in an offline forecasting comparison with a 24-hour timestamp lag. Exploratory validation compared local, centralized, Federated Averaging, and Federated Proximal (FedProx) training. FedProx (E = 1, mu = 1) was selected for a confirmatory comparison under a protocol fixed before test evaluation. The comparison used past-only offline inputs, five paired training seeds, macro-averaged mean absolute error (MAE), a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 0.005, and a paired day bootstrap with 10,000 repetitions over 49 test dates. Results: FedProx achieved a macro-MAE of 0.128397, compared with 0.133405 for centralized training. The paired difference (FedProx minus centralized) was -0.005008 (95% confidence interval: [-0.009926, -0.000537]). The upper confidence bound was below the prespecified margin, satisfying the non-inferiority criterion. All five seed-specific differences favored FedProx, and its mean MAE was lower at six of the seven stations. Post hoc calendar sensitivity analyses did not change the conclusion. Conclusions: These findings support further evaluation of federated forecasting for collaboration under data-pooling constraints. The study demonstrates predictive non-inferiority within the evaluated setting. Benefits for energy commitments and battery scheduling remain potential applications requiring operational evaluation.

title: Universal Analytical Description of Magnetoexcitons in Two-Dimensional Semiconducting Materials
abstract: Matching the Coulomb and logarithmic limits of the Rytova--Keldysh model gives a universal zero-field spectrum for monolayer exciton $s$ states, $E_n\simeq-\mathrm{Ry}^*/[n-1/2+f_n(ξ)]^2$, where $ξ$ is the screening parameter. Analytical radii determine diamagnetic coefficients and the magnetic crossover scale. Zero-field deviations peak near $1\%$ across the full screening range $0\leqξ\leq100$. For the sampled hBN-encapsulated monolayers, magnetoexciton energies agree with numerical spectra to sub-meV rms up to $100\T$ and capture the measured orbital shifts. Shared parameters link optical and magneto-optical spectra.

title: The integral role of artificial intelligence models in retinal detachment diagnostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: PurposeRetinal detachment (RD) is a vision-threatening condition requiring prompt diagnosis and management to optimize visual outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models have demonstrated promising results in RD detection across multiple imaging modalities; however, concerns regarding heterogeneity, external validation, and real-world implementation remain.
venue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
